title: Chanting at Senbon
translation: At Senbon there is a service where people chant the name of Shakyamuni, the historical Buddha. The priest Nyorin started it, around 1270.
original: {千本|せんぼん}の{釈迦念仏|しやかねんぶつ}は、{文永|ぶんえい}のころ、{如輪|じよりん}{上人|しやうにん}これを{始|はじ}められけり。
literal: The Shaka nenbutsu at Senbon was begun by the holy man Nyorin around the Bun'ei years.

notes.text: The temple Daihōonji, north-east of the Kitano shrine in the north-west of the capital, as the edition explains. It is still called the Senbon Shakadō.

{念仏|ねんぶつ} usually means calling on Amida (see sections 222 and 227). Here people call on Shaka, the historical Buddha, instead. The 1925 edition says the service ran from the ninth to the fifteenth of the third month; modern commentaries give the second month, around the anniversary of the Buddha's death (the fifteenth).
{文永|ぶんえい}: an era name, 1264–1275.

The 1925 edition identifies Nyorin as Chōkū, a disciple of Hōnen. Modern commentaries call him the second abbot of Daihōonji and a pupil of Hōnen's disciple Chōsai. {始|はじ}められけり: られ is respectful here, for the priest.
